key_concepts: Motion is a change in position relative to a reference point over time
Position is the location of an object at a particular time
A reference point is a fixed object used to describe motion
Distance is the total length of path travelled
Displacement is the overall change in position from the starting point
Distance is a scalar quantity with magnitude only
Displacement is a vector quantity with magnitude and direction
Displacement can be zero when an object returns to its starting point
Displacement equals distance when motion is along a straight line in one direction
To find distance, add all magnitudes of movement
To find displacement, combine same directions and subtract opposite directions
